summary:
We developed NASA’s Silent Space Heroes, an engaging, kid-friendly educational storytelling presentation designed specifically for school students.
To address the Abandoned, But Not Forgotten challenge, our project transforms complex NASA mission archives into an exciting visual journey across the Moon, Mars, and deep space. Using simple analogies, vibrant illustrations, and relatable storytelling, we introduce students to historic pioneers—from Apollo lunar landers and Mars rovers like Spirit, Opportunity, and Ingenuity, to deep-space probes like Voyager—while explaining space laws, space recycling, and planetary protection.
This project is important because young learners often find space science overly technical. By framing inactive spacecraft as heroic pioneers rather than "space trash"—and highlighting how iconic rovers were named by school students—we spark curiosity, preserve humanity’s cosmic heritage, and inspire the next generation of space explorers.
details:
What does it do & How does it work?

NASA’s Silent Space Heroes is an interactive, storytelling-based educational presentation that I developed individually for school students. It takes young learners on an exciting visual journey across the Moon, Mars, and interstellar space to explore NASA’s inactive landers, rovers, and orbital hardware. Each slide pairs vivid custom illustrations with my own authentic, narrative voiceover that brings historic missions—like Apollo, Viking, Spirit, Opportunity, InSight, Ingenuity, and Voyager—to life.

What benefits does it have & What is the intended impact?

The primary benefit of this project is making complex space science and space law accessible, fun, and memorable for children. My intended impact is to shift how young minds view inactive spacecraft—showing them that these machines are priceless historical monuments ("anthropogenic materials") rather than "space trash." By highlighting that famous Mars rovers were named by school students through essay contests, I aim to spark lifelong curiosity and inspire the next generation of space explorers.

How is the project creative?

As a solo creator, I transformed heavy scientific concepts into relatable, kid-friendly analogies—such as comparing space treaties to "museum velvet ropes," rover upgrades to "leveling up," and lunar artifacts to "hidden Easter eggs." Combining custom visual storytelling with a warm, engaging voiceover keeps students hooked from start to finish.

Tools, Software, Hardware & AI Used:

• Software & Hardware: Microsoft PowerPoint for slide design and audio recording (recorded directly using built-in device audio without external microphones), and Google Drive for cloud hosting.

• Use of Super Intelligence (AI Tools): ChatGPT and Google AI were used to refine my kid-friendly narration scripts and generate custom visual illustrations for the slides, while the presentation structure and voiceover recording were created manually by me.

• Official NASA & Partner Data Used: Official NASA Open Data & Mission Archives (Apollo Program, Mars Exploration Program, Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, and Voyager mission data) along with ISRO Chandrayaan mission resources.

What factors did I consider?

Working independently, I prioritized age-appropriate language, visual clarity, scientific accuracy, and global inclusivity. I carefully balanced official NASA mission facts with simple everyday comparisons so school children could easily understand complex topics like planetary protection, space weathering, and space recycling without feeling overwhelmed.
